q-156127.name: Question 1
q-156127.problem:
What is the solution to the following system of inequalities?

$$
\{\begin{aligned}n+2<5 \\ 1-2n\le 3\end{aligned}
$$
q-156127.worked_solution:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $n$ that satisfy both $n+2<5$ and $1-2n\le 3$ simultaneously.

- First, we solve $n+2<5\,:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}n+2 & <5 \\ n+2-2 & <5-2 \\ n & <3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/4e6e1c1a65abf5b7b88d39bb4d2606d64d5bc9ae526925e9f869eab0927194e3.png)

$$

$$

- Then, we solve $1-2n\le 3\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2n & \le 3 \\ 1-2n-1 & \le 3-1 \\ -2n & \le 2 \\ (-1)\cdot (-2n) & \ge (-1)\cdot 2 \\ 2n & \ge -2 \\ \frac{2n}{2} & \ge \frac{-2}{2} \\ n & \ge -1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/8e96c91b84e3c69b2e8f58251dbe21294ef8b23ffa695c1b7fbe53ad4f22b2fc.png)

To find the values of $n$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/cd1d2ad0e357eb3117e5b61351afeda01a348bfff5aec1a2d2940c77ecae120c.png)

 

$$

$$

Thus, the final solution is $n\in [-1,3).$

q-156128.name: Question 2
q-156128.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $1<2x-1\le 5$ and $1-2x\le 3.$
q-156128.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

- First, we solve $1<2x-1\le 5\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & <2x-1\le 5 \\ 1+1 & <2x-1+1\le 5+1 \\ 2 & <2x\le 6 \\ \frac{2}{2} & <\frac{2x}{2}\le \frac{6}{2} \\ 1 & <x\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/2b111554de3019b78a3d6e8992477bb1401a53d7c2bbe09a6407e675b8d06daa.png)

- Then, we solve  $1-2x\le 3\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2x & \le 3 \\ 1-2x-1 & \le 3-1 \\ -2x & \le 2 \\ (-1)\cdot (-2x) & \ge (-1)\cdot 2 \\ 2x & \ge -2 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & \ge \frac{-2}{2} \\ x & \ge -1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/ca4d8a229772ec9d22a45c99cdad22379b6b55aa5d6fe4bb6288fe66d8c5696a.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/74cc11cbd20e5b82171d4c89407f24eb6f60ee558bf41a313009839c6f885f7e.png)

 

$$

$$

Thus, the final solution is $x\in (1,3].$
